condition_or_topic: dissemination and implementation sciences in allergy and immunology
clinical_background: Translating evidence-based practices into real-world clinical settings is often slow and resource-intensive. In allergy and immunology, variations in knowledge, resources, patient populations, and staffing models lead to differences in care for asthma, allergic diseases, and primary immunodeficiency. Despite the need for validated approaches to study how to best apply evidence-based practices in the real world, dissemination and implementation (D&I) sciences are underutilized. Uptake of research innovations into clinical practice is low, with less than 50% of discoveries reaching real-world settings and a typical 17-year time lag. Adherence to clinical guidelines in allergy and immunology is variable and influenced by resource availability, preexisting health inequities, clinician preferences, and environmental factors.
objectives: To provide an overview of the role of dissemination and implementation sciences in clinical care and future research within allergy and immunology

To advocate for greater awareness and understanding of D&I sciences as distinct fields of study compared to quality improvement, practice improvement, health services research, and guideline development
To provide examples of where D&I sciences can improve care for patients with allergic and immunologic conditions
title: Applying the dissemination and implementation sciences to allergy and immunology: A Work Group Report from the AAAAI Quality, Adherence, and Outcomes Committee

interpretation: The dissemination and implementation (D&I) sciences are currently underutilized in allergy and immunology, yet they offer systematic and validated approaches to examine and close gaps between evidence-based guidelines and real-world delivery of care, with a strong emphasis on health equity, intervention fidelity, and sustainability.
clinical_implications: Application of D&I sciences can lead to more consistent delivery of evidence-based practices in asthma, allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, drug allergy, food allergy, and primary immunodeficiency by identifying and mitigating contextual barriers.
Integrating D&I frameworks into research and practice can help address observed health disparities in minoritized and underserved populations.
D&I approaches may improve the uptake of critical interventions such as early peanut introduction, penicillin allergy delabeling, and SMART therapy in asthma.
practice_implications: Allergists and immunologists should be receptive to practice changes informed by D&I study findings and actively leverage D&I research to develop and adapt healthcare interventions.
Clinicians and health systems should incorporate D&I frameworks when planning and evaluating the implementation of new guidelines or quality improvement initiatives.
Multidisciplinary teams that include community partners, patients, and diverse stakeholders are essential for successful D&I efforts.
Guideline developers should consider including implementation strategies and D&I principles to facilitate real-world adoption.
limitations: D&I studies can be expensive, particularly when multiple sites are involved, and may face competing operational pressures within health systems.
The variety of available D&I frameworks can be daunting, and selecting the most appropriate one requires expertise.
Without careful integration of a health equity lens, D&I research risks exacerbating existing disparities by favoring populations with greater access and health literacy.
The need for mixed methods, longitudinal data, and real-time EHR or digital data collection adds complexity to study design and execution.
strengths: D&I sciences provide a rigorous, systematic methodology to study not only clinical effectiveness but also reach, adoption, implementation fidelity, and sustainability of evidence-based practices.
The use of process, determinant, and evaluation frameworks (e.g., EPIS, CFIR, RE-AIM) offers structured roadmaps to guide implementation and assess contextual factors.
Mixed methods approaches allow for a comprehensive understanding of barriers and facilitators at individual, organizational, and system levels.
D&I research explicitly prioritizes health equity and can uncover how interventions affect historically marginalized populations differently.
open_questions: How can D&I frameworks be best adapted to the specific clinical settings and diverse populations encountered in allergy and immunology?
What funding mechanisms and institutional supports are most effective for sustaining D&I research in this field?
How can D&I studies effectively address structural barriers such as insurance coverage and FDA approval status that limit guideline implementation?
What strategies are most effective for de-implementing low-value or outdated practices, such as routine corticosteroid use in biphasic anaphylaxis prevention?
future_directions: Increase dedicated grant funding for D&I research in allergy and immunology from agencies such as NIH and PCORI.
Develop training and mentorship programs to build D&I science capacity among allergists, immunologists, and researchers.
Expand research networks to include implementation scientists and health disparities experts as core collaborators.
Integrate D&I considerations directly into the development and dissemination of clinical practice guidelines and practice parameters.
Conduct more pragmatic and hybrid effectiveness-implementation trials to accelerate translation of evidence into front-line practice.
Leverage D&I approaches to design and test interventions that specifically target health inequities in allergic and immunologic conditions.

tables.summary: This table lists various allergic and immunologic conditions along with their evidence-based practices and potential targets for implementation science interventions, including strategies for asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis, atopic dermatitis, drug allergy, food allergy, health disparities, school-based care coordination, and primary immunodeficiency.

main_conclusion: The dissemination and implementation (D&I) sciences provide essential frameworks to study and enhance the translation of evidence-based practices into real-world allergy and immunology care, promoting health equity and optimizing clinical outcomes through multidisciplinary collaboration and mixed-methods approaches.
narrative_summary: This work group report from the AAAAI Quality, Adherence, and Outcomes Committee examines the role of dissemination and implementation (D&I) sciences in allergy and immunology. Despite significant research investment, less than 50% of discoveries reach practice, with an average 17-year lag. D&I sciences use frameworks like EPIS, PRISM, and RE-AIM to systematically identify barriers and facilitators to adopting evidence-based practices. The report emphasizes the need for multidisciplinary teams, mixed-methods data, and stakeholder engagement from the outset. Key examples include school-based asthma programs, penicillin allergy delabeling, early peanut introduction, and SMART therapy for asthma. D&I sciences also offer tools to address health disparities by studying contextual factors and promoting equitable access to interventions. Allergists and immunologists are encouraged to incorporate D&I principles to accelerate the uptake of guidelines into practice, ensuring interventions are effective, sustainable, and equitable. Future directions include increased funding, training, and collaboration with implementation scientists to bridge the evidence-to-practice gap.

scales_and_classifications.name: EPIS (Exploration, Preparation, Implementation, Sustainment)
scales_and_classifications.description: Process framework used to guide the workflow for translating evidence-based practice into real-world settings.

scales_and_classifications.name: PRISM (Practical Implementation Sustainability Model)
scales_and_classifications.description: Process framework focusing on practical aspects of implementation and sustainability.

scales_and_classifications.name: RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance)
scales_and_classifications.description: Evaluation framework measuring key implementation outcomes.

scales_and_classifications.name: Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR)
scales_and_classifications.description: Determinant framework to understand factors influencing implementation, updated based on user feedback.

scales_and_classifications.name: Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF)
scales_and_classifications.description: Determinant framework used to identify barriers and facilitators to implementation.

scales_and_classifications.name: Health Equity Framework
scales_and_classifications.description: Framework integrating health equity into implementation research.

scales_and_classifications.name: Equity-Based Framework for Implementation Research
scales_and_classifications.description: Framework used to promote equity-focused implementation research.

scales_and_classifications.name: GRADE (Grades of Recommendation Assessment, Development, and Evaluation)
scales_and_classifications.description: System for grading clinical practice guidelines.

scales_and_classifications.name: PDSA (plan-do-study-act)
scales_and_classifications.description: Quality improvement cycle approach for iterative intervention improvement.
